title: Bhopal, 23 July 1955: How the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh began
author: Editorial Desk
summary: A small gathering in Bhopal, a birth anniversary of Lokmanya Tilak, and a union with not one registered affiliate.
body:
Most large organisations start with a split from an older one. The Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh did not. It began on **23 July 1955** at Bhopal, when a small group of invitees from different parts of the country met and announced a new national trade union centre.

## Why that date

BMS records that 23 July was chosen because it is the birth anniversary of **Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, the veteran of the freedom movement. The founding is associated with **Dattopant Thengadi**, a Sangh pracharak who had spent years learning how existing unions worked.

## From nothing

A BMS history titled *The Onward March of BMS* notes a striking fact: on the day of its founding, BMS had **not a single registered union affiliated to it**. It had to begin from scratch. At that time, the recognised central labour organisations were closely tied to political parties or groups. BMS set out to be an independent, nationalist alternative that was constructive, not merely agitational. It argued that industrial peace was a precondition for industrial progress.

## What came next

The early karyakartas were mostly social workers with little trade-union experience. They learnt as they went. Within about three decades, according to writers who have followed the movement, BMS grew to become the largest central trade union organisation in India. Today BMS describes itself as India's largest national trade union centre.

The story of Bhopal is worth remembering for one reason above all: **patient work at the base** built what a declaration alone could not.

In coming weeks this blog will look at the thinking behind that founding, the man who led it, and the road since.
